page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered to deliver dedicated GPU resources alongside balanced general compute capacity. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the platform is driven by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor utilizing x86_64 architecture with 4 vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is anchored by an NVIDIA T4 GPU from the Turing family, providing 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Storage includes 125 GB of local NVMe SSD space alongside 5 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Standard host-level benchmark scores place the general compute and memory subsystems in the lower performance brackets. Multi-core and single-core metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench rank within the bottom 25%, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 2540.0 and PassMark CPU scoring 3960.76. Host memory bandwidth remains modest, measuring 26.46 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 22.4 GB/sec for writes. In contrast, the dedicated NVIDIA T4 accelerator exhibits substantial throughput in targeted machine learning evaluations. Prompt processing for small 135M language models achieves top-tier throughput at 8,457.62 tokens per second, while medium 7B models sustain 1,163.27 tokens per second. Generation speeds for 7B models hold strong at 40.68 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4dn.xlarge serves as a resource-dense, economical entry point for GPU-assisted computation where full host-CPU saturation is unnecessary. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio accommodates typical runtime dependencies, while bundled local NVMe storage reduces external disk latency for caching datasets and model weights. The system is ill-suited for dense CPU-bound compile clusters or 70B parameter models exceeding the 16 GB VRAM threshold. Its hardware balance is specifically aligned with small-to-medium machine learning model inference, remote graphic workstations, video transcoding, and GPU-accelerated data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services g4dn.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for GPU-driven workloads such as machine learning inference and graphics processing. The instance features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor offering 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 16 GB of DDR4 system memory. Acceleration is provided by a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, complemented by 125 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. While general-purpose CPU and memory throughput benchmark within the lower 25th percentile, the accelerator delivers top-tier prompt processing and strong generation speeds for small and medium language models. This configuration offers a cost-effective platform for lightweight AI inference, media processing, and visual computing where heavy host-side compute capacity is not required.
